items.record:
# Dev recovery test #2 — 2026-08-28

## Summary
**FAILED** at the secrets layer (runbook step 7 / L3). Platform and data layers came up; the business success bar was never reached cleanly.

- T0 (first failover action): 14:02 UTC
- First access to recovered cluster: 14:31 UTC (29 min)
- T1 declared at 14:49 UTC — **but only for the edge healthcheck**. The claim path never answered. RTA 47 min is therefore the *platform* RTA, not a business RTA. cleanRun = false.
- Measured RPA: **118 min**, on the remittance Aurora — the one Tier-0 store still on third-party point-in-time recovery (configured at 30 min). The adjudication global cluster failed over with sub-second lag. Those two numbers side by side are the whole argument in dec_mechanisms: continuous replication gives you a *current* copy; a recovery point gives you a *consistent moment*, which may be two hours old. The object and queue recovery points came from a different sync than the database one — alignment was assumed, not checked.
- **Read 118 as an upper bound, not a measurement.** The freshness query we ran was `SELECT now() - max(settled_at)`, and the restored remittance database took no writes during the test, so that expression returns the recovery-point age PLUS however long the test had been running when we ran it — and we ran it roughly 90 minutes in. Part of the 118 may be the clock, not the data. It does not change the finding (the points were not aligned and 30 min was not achieved) but it does change what we are entitled to say the number is. Test #3 records `max(settled_at)` as a timestamp and subtracts T0.

## The ugly parts
1. `adjudication/partner-api-key` and one KMS-wrapped credential had no replica in us-east-2. secrets-init crash-looped for ~35 minutes while we debugged the *app*, because the pod error said `CreateContainerError`, not "missing secret". A replica secret keeps the same name, so a name that resolves in us-east-1 and not in us-east-2 means nobody ever enabled replication for it. The three lists (secrets actually marked for replication, the spreadsheet, the runtime logical names) still disagree — this is now blocker gap gap_secrets1.
2. Cold start: 40+ min from the recovery-region apply to pods Ready. Karpenter had to build every node from scratch and image pulls were serial. ACME-DR-232 tracks pre-warming options.
3. We nearly triggered failback at teardown out of habit — on a real global cluster, which would have been a real switchover. The 'no failback without approval' rule exists because of this moment; it is now a gate in the runbook.
4. **The worst thing in this record is the thing nobody wrote down at the time.** Runbook step 6 told us to fail the adjudication Aurora global cluster over to us-east-2, and we did — a Tier-0 production cluster, inside a test whose own notes said "DNS and live traffic untouched". Because DNS was untouched, the us-east-1 pods kept serving and their writes started failing the moment the failover completed; because it was a *failover* and not a switchover, the old writer was not demoted and we chose to lose the unreplicated tail on purpose, in a planned drill where both regions were healthy and a switchover would have been RPO 0; and because the rollback was `terragrunt run-all destroy`, there was no step that ever returned the writer. This was a production incident dressed as a test. It is written up on 2026-09-17 as dec_nopromote, the runbook's data gate has been rewritten (stp_a06 measures the lag and promotes nothing; stp_a06b restores a writable drill copy for the success bar), and the rollback now opens with stp_r00 — establish who holds the writer, and return it by graceful switchover before anything is destroyed.

## What passed
ECR replication had every image in us-east-2 before anything needed one, and all pods pulled from the recovery-region registry. Objects written that morning were already replicated (the pre-CRR backlog is still an open hole — nothing written before the rule existed is over there). The adjudication global cluster failed over cleanly and answered freshness queries. Edge chain (API GW → VPC Link → NLB) returned 200 with the Host header.

## Follow-ups
- Reconcile secret lists to ONE signed-off CSV and verify each entry has a replica (gap_secrets1, ACME-DR-231) — owner: platform.
- Recovery-point alignment check added as runbook step 1 gate, alongside per-mechanism lag checks (gap_rpa1, ACME-DR-233).
- Next test (#3) scheduled 2026-09-25; entry criterion: signed-off secret list verified in us-east-2.

items.name: Dev recovery test #3 — September
items.scope: Repeat of test #2 with the reconciled secret list, on the rewritten runbook. Entry criteria: Phase 0 checklist green, signed-off secrets verified to have replicas in us-east-2, every replication path checked current, and the two point-in-time recovery points aligned. Success bar unchanged: claim adjudicated end-to-end + settlement import, direct endpoints only, no DNS changes. CHANGED SINCE #2: the production adjudication global cluster is NOT promoted (dec_nopromote) — its RPA is the replica lag at T0 and the success bar writes to a restored drill cluster (stp_a06b). NOT COVERED by this test, and still open after a green run: the partner clearinghouse path, because containment is ON and the recovery-region egress allowlist is a manual support ticket (gap_partner1); and the public DNS cutover (gap_dns1).

appTests.name: Claim submitted returns a business response (not a 500)
Secrets readable by the app role in the recovery region
appTests.command: kubectl --context <recovery-ctx> exec -n claims deploy/adjudication -- sh -c 'aws sts get-caller-identity; aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id adjudication/db-password --query SecretString --output text >/dev/null && echo DECRYPT_OK'
appTests.expected: caller is the app role and every signed-off secret returns DECRYPT_OK

appTests.name: Images pulled from recovery-region registry (initContainers included)
appTests.command: kubectl --context <recovery-ctx> get pods -A -o jsonpath over .spec.initContainers[*].image and .spec.containers[*].image | sort -u
appTests.expected: all images from us-east-2 registry, secrets-init among them

appTests.name: Aurora global cluster replica lag at T0 (measures RPA for claims — no promotion)
appTests.command: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/RDS --metric-name AuroraGlobalDBReplicationLag --region us-east-2 (and describe-global-clusters to confirm the writer is still us-east-1)
appTests.expected: lag under a minute at T0, and the writer member ARN is still the us-east-1 cluster

appTests.name: Adjudication writes land in the drill copy, not in production
appTests.command: psql -h <drill-writer-endpoint> -c "SELECT claim_id, created_at FROM claims ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1"
appTests.expected: the claim_id returned by the success-bar call is the newest row in the DRILL cluster

appTests.name: Remittance freshness query (measures RPA for the point-in-time store)
appTests.command: psql: SELECT max(settled_at) FROM remittances — RPA = T0 minus that timestamp, never now() minus it
appTests.expected: newest row within 30 min of T0 (aligned points)

appTests.name: S3 objects written since the last backfill are present in the recovery bucket
appTests.expected: object present; ReplicationStatus COMPLETED on the source

appTests.name: Edge reachable via direct endpoint + Host header
Recovered API authorizer issues and accepts a token WITHOUT calling the partner (containment stays ON)
appTests.command: client_credentials grant against the recovered authorizer via the direct execute-api endpoint; no partner-issued token, no partner endpoint contacted
appTests.expected: token issued and accepted by the recovered authorizer; the containment probe still reports zero reachable partner endpoints

appTests.name: Partner clearinghouse path — NOT EXERCISED, and deliberately so
appTests.command: not run: containment is ON and the recovery-region egress IPs are not on the clearinghouse allowlist (gap_partner1, ACME-DR-228)
appTests.expected: recorded as unproven; a green test does not mean claims would reach the partner from us-east-2
